body.text: Why Fences in This Region Turn Grey So Fast

Wood fences in Kitchener-Waterloo pick up a grey, weathered look faster than most homeowners expect, usually within a year or two of installation if they were never sealed. The humidity that rolls through Southwestern Ontario in summer, combined with tree cover in older neighbourhoods and shaded side yards that never fully dry out, gives mildew and algae plenty to work with. Vinyl and composite fences do not grey the same way, but they collect the same grime, pollen and green staining along the base where grass clippings and sprinkler overspray sit against the panel. Whatever the material, a build-up of dirt and organic growth is one of the fastest ways to make an otherwise solid fence look neglected.
How We Clean Wood, Vinyl and Composite Differently

A fence is not a driveway, and treating it like one is how amateur pressure washing gouges wood fibres or blasts vinyl panels loose from their rails. We start every job by identifying the material and its condition, then set the equipment accordingly.

items: Cedar and pressure-treated wood get lower pressure and a longer dwell time for the cleaning solution to do the work
Vinyl fencing gets a wider fan tip and moderate pressure to avoid driving water behind the panels
Composite fencing is cleaned similarly to vinyl, watching for any joints or caps that could trap moisture
Heavily weathered or older wood is cleaned more conservatively to avoid raising the grain excessively

body.text: Cleaning Before Staining: Why Order Matters

If a fence cleaning is step one before staining, we treat it that way from the start. Grey, weathered wood has a compromised surface layer that will not accept stain evenly, so a proper clean opens the grain back up and gives the new coat something to bond to. This is one of the reasons a rushed cleaning job leads to blotchy staining later. See /fence-staining and /fence-painting for what typically comes next once your fence is clean and dry.

A large share of the fence cleaning calls we get in Kitchener, Waterloo and Cambridge involve a shared boundary fence where only one side wants the work done. That is a routine situation for us. We stay on your side of the property line, keep spray and runoff contained as much as possible, and let you know ahead of time if the job requires brief access from the neighbouring yard. Most jobs do not, and we have done enough of these to know how to get a thorough clean without turning it into a conversation with the neighbours.
Equipment and Technique Matter More Than Raw Pressure

Homeowners renting a pressure washer from a hardware store often assume more pressure means a better result, and that assumption is exactly how fences get damaged. A consumer machine held too close to a cedar panel will strip fibres and leave a fuzzy, damaged surface that no longer takes stain evenly. We use commercial-grade equipment with adjustable pressure and interchangeable tips, holding a consistent distance and angle across the whole fence line rather than concentrating pressure on stubborn spots, which is usually how gouging happens. Technique, not brute force, is what actually lifts dirt and mildew cleanly.
How Often a Fence Actually Needs Cleaning

Most wood fences in our service area benefit from a clean every two to three years, though a fence under heavy tree cover or facing north where it stays shaded and damp may need attention more often. Vinyl and composite fences can typically go longer between cleanings since they do not absorb moisture the way wood does, but a yearly rinse keeps pollen and green algae from building up at the base.

If your fence is due for a re-stain, book the cleaning and staining together. Cleaning first thing in the visit gives the wood time to dry before we apply stain later the same day or the next, which keeps the whole project moving.

Fence cleaning is typically priced by linear footage and is often bundled with staining or painting for better overall value. A stand-alone clean for a standard residential fence in Kitchener-Waterloo generally runs in the $800 to $1,200 range depending on length, condition and access. We give an exact number after seeing the fence, not a guess over the phone.

faqs.q: How often should a fence be cleaned?
faqs.a: Most wood fences in this region need cleaning every two to three years, though shaded or heavily treed properties may need it more often. Vinyl and composite fences can usually go longer between cleanings.

faqs.q: Can you clean vinyl and composite fences, or just wood?
faqs.a: We clean all three. Vinyl and composite need lower pressure and a different technique than wood, so we adjust our equipment and approach to the material.

faqs.q: What if my neighbour does not want their side of a shared fence cleaned?
faqs.a: We can clean just your side of a shared boundary fence, staying within your property line and keeping the job contained so the neighbouring yard is barely affected.

faqs.q: Is the cleaning solution safe for my garden and pets?
faqs.a: Yes. We use plant-safe, VOC-compliant cleaning solutions and take care to protect garden beds and landscaping along the fence line before we start.

faqs.q: Do I need to clean my fence before staining it?
faqs.a: Yes. Stain applied over a dirty or weathered surface will not penetrate evenly and often looks blotchy within a season. Cleaning is the first step in every staining or painting job we do.
